title: Longest increasing subsequence
statement: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence. n up to 5 × 10⁴, so O(n²) is too slow in Python.
hints: O(n²): dp[i] = 1 + max dp[j] over j < i with nums[j] < nums[i].
O(n log n): tails[k] = the smallest possible tail of an increasing subsequence of length k + 1; binary search where x goes.

solution.explanation: The O(n²) DP is the one to explain first. The speed-up changes the state: instead of "the best length ending at i", keep tails[k] = the smallest tail of any increasing subsequence of length k + 1. tails is strictly increasing, so each x replaces the first tail ≥ x (bisect_left), or extends the list. Smaller tails can only help later. The array is not itself an LIS; only its length is meaningful.
